claim: N3 PCIe post-host-init IRQ setup releases host resources on IRQ/action failure and on device teardown; shared IRQ handler only acknowledges its MSI bit.
oracle: Actual helper fault injection proves request failure -> host deinit once; action-registration failure -> stop_children/mask/free_irq/host_deinit once; normal teardown same order; unrelated IRQ -> IRQ_NONE and no acknowledgement; actual kernel W=1 build/modpost passes.

user_journey.scenario: A future WiFi startup fails or device driver is removed: the phone must retain its recovery path without leaked PCI host/clocks/PHY or stale channel pointer.
user_journey.expected: Failure is visible and resource ownership released; hardware recovery still requires subsequent device test.

invariants: Stop PCI child drivers while IRQ handler is still available; then mask/free IRQ before removing DWC domain. Kernel pci_stop_dev skips already-stopped devices when DWC repeats stop_root_bus.
DWC host_init owns cleanup on its own failures; our helper only runs after it returns0
Mask own MSI gate before freeing IRQ; free_irq synchronizes handlers before DWC MSI domain removal
No devm_request_irq double ownership; one devres cleanup action owns successful request_irq
Initial MSI gate stays masked until handler and cleanup action are installed
Clear registry only if this device owns it
Do not acknowledge unrelated IRQ bits or claim shared interrupts without MSI status
